table.name: atom
table.purpose: One row per atom in a chemical structure dataset: each atom is identified within its molecule (TR###_n), carries its chemical element, and links to its parent molecule via molecule_id. Atoms are connected to each other through the connected table (which references atom_id from both sides), and bonds are described in the bond table.

atom_id.name: atom_id
atom_id.description: Unique identifier of an atom; composed of the parent molecule code (e.g. TR031) plus an underscore and a per-molecule atom index (e.g. _31). Primary key of the atom table; referenced by connected.atom_id and connected.atom_id2.

element.name: element
element.description: Chemical element symbol of the atom, lowercase (h = hydrogen, c = carbon, o = oxygen, n = nitrogen, cl = chlorine, etc.; 21 distinct elements including p, zn, br, si).

molecule_id.name: molecule_id
molecule_id.description: Identifier of the molecule the atom belongs to; foreign key to molecule.molecule_id. Each atom belongs to exactly one molecule (444 molecules, up to ~174 atoms each).

table.name: bond
table.purpose: Chemical bonds between atoms in molecules. Each row is one bond in one molecule, linking two atoms (identified by their indices in bond_id) with a bond order (single, double, or triple). The bond_id atom indices presumably join to atom records via the 'connected' table, which references bond_id.

bond_id.name: bond_id
bond_id.description: Primary key identifying a chemical bond. Encoded as <molecule_id>_<atom_index_1>_<atom_index_2>, where the two numbers are the indices of the bonded atoms within the molecule (e.g. TR365_13_14 is the bond between atoms 13 and 14 of molecule TR365).

bond_type.name: bond_type
bond_type.description: Bond order notation in standard chemical notation: '-' = single bond (10528 rows), '=' = double bond (1844 rows), '#' = triple bond (6 rows).

molecule_id.name: molecule_id
molecule_id.description: Foreign key to molecule.molecule_id; the molecule (TR-prefixed code) that contains this bond. Each molecule has multiple bonds (444 molecules, 12379 bonds).

table.name: connected
table.purpose: Edge/association table linking pairs of atoms to the bond between them: each row states that atom atom_id and atom atom_id2 are joined by bond bond_id. It materializes the atom–bond–atom relationship (likely one row per bond endpoint, so each bond appears twice with endpoints swapped), enabling traversal of molecular connectivity between the atom and bond tables.

atom_id.name: atom_id
atom_id.description: First atom of a bonded pair. Composite key with atom_id2 and bond_id; each row represents one connection between two atoms. Values are molecule-prefixed atom identifiers (e.g. TR018_11 = atom 11 of molecule TR018). References atom.atom_id.

atom_id2.name: atom_id2
atom_id2.description: Second atom of the bonded pair; references atom.atom_id. Together with atom_id it identifies the two endpoints of the bond referenced by bond_id.

bond_id.name: bond_id
bond_id.description: Identifier of the bond connecting atom_id and atom_id2; references bond.bond_id. Encoded as <molecule>_<atom1>_<atom2> (e.g. TR018_11_12). Duplicated values (top count 2) suggest each bond appears twice, once per direction/endpoint ordering.

table.name: molecule
table.purpose: One row per molecule in a chemical structure dataset. Each molecule has a unique ID (TRnnn) and a charge sign label ('+' cation or '-' anion). Its atoms and bonds are stored in the atom and bond tables, linked via molecule_id; the 'connected' table likely records connectivity between molecules or components.

label.name: charge_sign
label.description: Charge sign of the molecule: '-' for negatively charged (anionic) molecules, '+' for positively charged (cationic) molecules. Binary flag, 191 negative vs 152 positive.

molecule_id.name: molecule_id
molecule_id.description: Primary key identifying each molecule, formatted as 'TR' followed by a zero-padded number (e.g. TR000, TR477). Referenced by atom.molecule_id and bond.molecule_id, which store the atoms and bonds belonging to each molecule.
